mainTopic: The ארון's journeys, the stones set up when entering ארץ ישראל, and how the Torah was written on them
overview: This amud finishes the story of the people of בית שמש, who spoke to the ארון in a mocking way and were punished. רבי אבהו and רבי אלעזר explain the puzzling numbers 'seventy men, fifty thousand men.' Next, two פסוקים give different offerings for when דוד brought the ארון to ירושלים. רב פפא בר שמואל and then רב חסדא explain that both offerings were brought, at different intervals. רבי יוחנן explains why the place where עוזא died is called both 'כידון' and 'נכון.' The גמרא then lists three sets of stones set up by משה and יהושע. A ברייתא brings a מחלוקת between רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון about whether the Torah was written under the plaster or on top of it, and how the nations could learn it. Each side reads the פסוק 'משרפות סיד' in its own way. The amud ends by asking which view a ברייתא about accepting repentant כנענים follows, and the answer comes on the next amud.

steps.title: The disrespectful words of the people of בית שמש to the ארון
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes quoting what the people of בית שמש said to the ארון when it returned from the פלשתים.
steps.simpleTranslation: Who made you so angry that you became angry, and who came to you so that you calmed down?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing the quote of what the people of בית שמש said to the ארון. They spoke to it in a mocking, careless way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: They talked to the ארון as if it were a person who got upset and then calmed down. This flippant attitude toward the קדושה of the ארון is the reason for the punishment described in the next step.

phrases.english: Who angered you, so that you became angry?
phrases.notes: Some versions leave out the word in round brackets. Either way, they are speaking to the ארון.

phrases.english: And who came to you, so that you were calmed down?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the quote of the people of בית שמש, continuing from the earlier part of the daf.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The people of בית שמש spoke to the ארון in a mocking way, as if it had been angry and then calmed down.

steps.title: How many people were struck: seventy or fifty thousand?
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבהו and רבי אלעזר explain why the פסוק gives two numbers for the people who were struck.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says: 'And He struck among the people seventy men, fifty thousand men.' רבי אבהו and רבי אלעזר disagree. One says there were seventy men, and each one was as important as fifty thousand. The other says there were fifty thousand men, and each one was as important as the seventy members of the סנהדרין.
steps.whatsHappening: The פסוק gives two numbers for how many people were struck, which is confusing. Two אמוראים each explain which number is the real count and what the other number means.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both opinions agree that one number is the actual count and the other number describes how important each person was. They only disagree about which number is which. Either way, the people who were punished were very important people.

keyTerms.meaning: Equal in worth, as important as
The great court of seventy judges

phrases.english: "And He struck among the people seventy men,
fifty thousand men."
Rabbi Abbahu and Rabbi Elazar disagree.
One says: there were seventy men,

phrases.aramaic: וְכׇל אֶחָד וְאֶחָד שָׁקוּל כַּחֲמִשִּׁים אֶלֶף.
phrases.english: and each and every one was equal to fifty thousand.
And one says: there were fifty thousand men,

phrases.aramaic: וְכׇל אֶחָד וְאֶחָד שָׁקוּל כְּשִׁבְעִים סַנְהֶדְרִין.
phrases.english: and each and every one was equal to the seventy of the Sanhedrin.

steps.whatToRemember: The פסוק's two numbers are explained as one real count plus a measure of how important each person was. רבי אבהו and רבי אלעזר just switch which is which.
steps.triggerLanguage: ויך בעם שבעים איש חמשים אלף איש
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Describes the punishment that came because of the disrespect in step 1.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One number in the פסוק is the actual count, and the other tells how important each person was. The two אמוראים disagree about which number is which.

steps.title: Two פסוקים give different counts of the offerings
steps.stepSummary: One פסוק says an ox and a fatling were brought after six steps, but another says seven bulls and seven rams.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says: 'When the carriers of the ארון of ה׳ had walked six steps, he sacrificed an ox and a fatling.' But another פסוק says: 'seven bulls and seven rams.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to דוד bringing the ארון to ירושלים and points out that two פסוקים give different offerings. This sets up the question that the next steps will answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two פסוקים describe the same event but list different animals and different amounts. The גמרא needs a way to make both true.

keyTerms.meaning: And it is written (introduces a second פסוק)

phrases.english: "And it was, when those who carried the Ark of the Lord had walked
six steps, he sacrificed an ox and a fatling."
And it is written: "seven bulls and seven rams."

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא never says 'there is a contradiction' out loud. Just putting the two פסוקים side by side is how it raises the question.
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic about the ארון: דוד's offerings as it was carried.
steps.kashyaTarget: How many offerings were brought while the ארון was carried
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: One פסוק says an ox and a fatling, and the other says seven bulls and seven rams. Both cannot simply be describing the same single offering.

steps.title: רב פפא בר שמואל: both offerings happened, at different intervals
steps.stepSummary: An ox and a fatling were brought for every step, and seven bulls and seven rams for every six steps.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא בר שמואל says: for every single step they brought an ox and a fatling, and for every six steps they brought seven bulls and seven rams.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא בר שמואל solves the problem by saying both פסוקים are right, because each describes a different kind of offering brought at a different interval.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The small offering, an ox and a fatling, was brought often, after every step. The big offering, seven bulls and seven rams, was brought after every six steps. Since they happened at different points, the two פסוקים no longer clash.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa bar Shmuel says:

phrases.aramaic: עַל כׇּל פְּסִיעָה וּפְסִיעָה שׁוֹר וּמְרִיא,
phrases.english: For each and every step, an ox and a fatling;
for every six steps,
seven bulls and seven rams.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the clash between the two פסוקים in step 3.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Both sources are true; they describe different offerings brought at different intervals.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two פסוקים seem to describe one offering in two different ways.
steps.terutzMaskana: Ox and fatling after every step; seven bulls and seven rams after every six steps.

steps.title: רב חסדא: that would mean far too many altars
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא objects that an offering at every step would fill ארץ ישראל with altars.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said to him: If so, you have filled all of ארץ ישראל with altars!
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא challenges רב פפא בר שמואל's answer by showing that it leads to a result that makes no sense.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If they stopped to bring an offering after every single step, they would have needed an altar at almost every step of the road. That is far too many to be realistic, so רב פפא בר שמואל's intervals cannot be right.

keyTerms.meaning: If so (introduces a problem with what was just said)

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב חִסְדָּא: אִם כֵּן,
phrases.english: Rav Ḥisda said to him: If so,

phrases.aramaic: מִילֵּאתָ אֶת כׇּל אֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל בָּמוֹת!
phrases.english: you have filled all of Eretz Yisrael with altars!

steps.triggerLanguage: אמר ליה רב חסדא אם כן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רב פפא בר שמואל's answer from step 4.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב פפא בר שמואל's claim that an ox and a fatling were brought at every single step
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: An offering at every step would need an altar at every step, filling the whole land with altars, which is unreasonable.

steps.title: רב חסדא: the offerings were spaced more widely
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא says an ox and a fatling were brought every six steps, and seven bulls and seven rams every six sets of six steps.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רב חסדא said: for every six steps, an ox and a fatling; for every six sets of six steps, seven bulls and seven rams.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא gives his own answer to the clash between the פסוקים, spacing the offerings farther apart so there are far fewer altars.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He keeps רב פפא בר שמואל's basic idea that both offerings were brought at different intervals, but stretches each interval six times longer. This also fits the פסוק's words 'six steps' directly with the ox and fatling.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather (rejects the earlier view and gives a new one)

phrases.english: Rather, Rav Ḥisda said:

phrases.aramaic: עַל כׇּל שֵׁשׁ וְשֵׁשׁ פְּסִיעוֹת — שׁוֹר וּמְרִיא,
phrases.english: For every six steps, an ox and a fatling;

phrases.aramaic: עַל כׇּל שִׁשָּׁה סְדָרִים שֶׁל שֵׁשׁ פְּסִיעוֹת —
phrases.english: for every six sets of six steps,
seven bulls and seven rams.

steps.whatToRemember: Both פסוקים are true because two kinds of offerings were brought at different intervals. רב חסדא spaces them out (every 6 steps and every 36 steps) so the land is not filled with altars.
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces רב פפא בר שמואל's answer after the problem raised in step 5.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Same idea of different intervals, but with wider spacing that avoids the problem of too many altars.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Offerings after every step and after every six steps (רב פפא בר שמואל).
steps.terutzMaskana: Ox and fatling every six steps; seven bulls and seven rams every thirty-six steps.

steps.title: Two Different Names for the Same Threshing Floor
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points out that one פסוק calls the place where עוזא died 'כידון' and another calls it 'נכון'.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is written 'כידון,' and it is written 'נכון.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא notices that two פסוקים tell the same story but give the place two different names. It is setting up a question that רבי יוחנן will answer next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both פסוקים describe the threshing floor where עוזא died while the ארון was being moved. Since it is the same event, two different names look like a contradiction that needs explaining.

keyTerms.meaning: כידון; the word also means a spear or javelin
נכון; the word also means settled or established

phrases.english: It is written "Chidon,"
and it is written "Nachon."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another contradiction between פסוקים about moving the ארון, like the ones in the earlier steps.
steps.kashyaTarget: The name of the threshing floor where עוזא died
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Two פסוקים describing one event give two different names for the same place.

steps.title: First a Spear, Then Settled
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן explains that both names describe the ארון at different times: at first it was like a spear, and in the end it was settled.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן says: At first it was 'כידון,' a spear, and in the end it was 'נכון,' settled.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן answers the contradiction. Each name is a description of a different stage, not a different place.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The names are read for their meaning. 'כידון' (spear) fits the beginning, when the ארון caused עוזא's death. 'נכון' (settled) fits the end, when it came to rest calmly. So both פסוקים are correct, and each one stresses a different part of the story.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan says:
At first it was "Chidon" (a spear),
phrases.notes: At first the ארון was dangerous like a spear, since עוזא died there.

phrases.english: and in the end it was "Nachon" (settled).

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: בַּתְּחִלָּה כִּידוֹן, וּלְבַסּוֹף נָכוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in step 7.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Both names are correct, and each describes a different stage of time
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two פסוקים disagree about the name of the place.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'כידון' describes the start, when the ארון was dangerous. 'נכון' describes the end, when it was settled.

steps.title: Three Sets of Stones, Starting with משה's Set in מואב
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא states that there were three sets of stones. The first was set up by משה in ארץ מואב, which is learned from a גזירה שוה on the word 'באר'.
steps.simpleTranslation: You find that you say there were three sets of stones. One was set up by משה in ארץ מואב, as it says: 'Beyond the ירדן, in the land of מואב, משה began to explain,' and further on it says: 'You shall write on them all the words of this Torah [very clearly].' This is learned from 'באר' and 'באר.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the topic of crossing into ארץ ישראל and says there were three sets of stones. It starts with the first set, which משה set up.
steps.deeperAnalysis: No פסוק says outright that משה wrote the Torah on stones. The גמרא learns it from a matching word: 'באר' is used for משה explaining the Torah in מואב, and the same word is used for writing the Torah on the stones. The shared word links the two, so משה also wrote the Torah on stones.

keyTerms.meaning: You find that you say (sums up what comes out of the פסוקים)
And it is learned (here, through a גזירה שוה)

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix this up with the stones written on at הר עיבל. This first set is the one משה himself set up earlier, in ארץ מואב, before the people crossed the ירדן.

phrases.english: You find that you say
there were three sets of stones:
one that Moshe set up in the land of Moav,
as it is stated:
"Beyond the Jordan, in the land of Moav,"
"Moshe began to explain, etc."
and further on it says:

phrases.aramaic: ״וְכָתַבְתָּ עֲלֵיהֶן אֶת כׇּל דִּבְרֵי הַתּוֹרָה הַזֹּאת וְגוֹ׳״,
phrases.english: "And you shall write on them all the words of this Torah, etc."
phrases.notes: דברים 27:8. The 'etc.' hides the key word: the פסוק ends 'בַּאֵר הֵיטֵב', meaning 'very clearly'.

phrases.english: and it is learned from "be'er" and "be'er."
phrases.notes: The same word appears in both פסוקים, so we connect them: משה also wrote the Torah on stones.

steps.triggerLanguage: נִמְצֵאתָ אַתָּה אוֹמֵר שְׁלֹשָׁה מִינֵי אֲבָנִים הָיוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the larger topic of bringing the ארון into ארץ ישראל and the stones set up at that time.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: There were three sets of stones. The first was set up by משה in ארץ מואב, and the Torah was written on it, as learned from the matching word 'באר'.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the list of three sets of stones that the next step finishes.

steps.title: יהושע's Stones in the ירדן and in the גלגל
steps.stepSummary: The second set was set up by יהושע inside the ירדן, and the third set was set up in the גלגל, each with its own פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: And one was set up by יהושע inside the ירדן, as it says: 'And twelve stones יהושע set up in the midst of the ירדן.' And one was set up in the גלגל, as it says: 'And these twelve stones which they took, etc.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes its list of three sets of stones. It brings a פסוק for the second set and for the third set.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both of these sets are written openly in ספר יהושע, so no special derivation is needed. One set of twelve stones stood inside the ירדן. A separate set of twelve stones, taken out of the ירדן, was set up in the גלגל. Together with משה's set, that makes three.

keyTerms.meaning: גלגל, the first camp after crossing the ירדן

steps.whatToRemember: Three sets of stones: (1) משה in ארץ מואב, learned from 'באר' and 'באר'; (2) יהושע inside the ירדן; (3) the stones set up in the גלגל.

phrases.english: And one that Yehoshua set up inside the Jordan,
as it is stated:
"And twelve stones"
"Yehoshua set up in the midst of the Jordan."
And one that he set up in Gilgal,
as it is stated:
"And these twelve stones"
"which they took, etc."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the list of three sets of stones begun in step 9.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The second set was in the ירדן and the third set was in the גלגל, both set up by יהושע.

steps.title: How the Torah Was Written on the Stones
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא asks how the Jewish people wrote the Torah. רבי יהודה says they wrote it on the stones and afterward covered them with plaster.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: How did the Jewish people write the Torah? רבי יהודה says: They wrote it on stones, as it says: 'And you shall write on the stones all the words of this Torah.' And afterward they plastered them over with plaster.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that asks how the Torah was actually written on the stones. רבי יהודה gives his view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה says the writing went directly onto the stones themselves, based on the plain words 'write on the stones'. Only after the writing was done were the stones covered with plaster. This order matters: the plaster came last, on top of the writing.

keyTerms.meaning: On top of the stones, directly on them
They plastered them over with plaster

steps.confusionAlert: In רבי יהודה's view the plaster goes on after the writing, covering it. Don't picture writing on top of the plaster.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
How did the Jewish people write the Torah?
Rabbi Yehuda says:
They wrote it on the stones,
as it is stated:
"And you shall write on the stones"

phrases.aramaic: אֶת כׇּל דִּבְרֵי הַתּוֹרָה הַזֹּאת וְגוֹ׳״,
phrases.english: "all the words of this Torah, etc."
And afterward they plastered them over with plaster.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: כֵּיצַד כָּתְבוּ יִשְׂרָאֵל אֶת הַתּוֹרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After listing the stones, the גמרא moves on to how the Torah was written on them.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי יהודה, the Torah was written directly on the stones, and the stones were then covered with plaster.
steps.whyThisMatters: This opens a ברייתא about how the writing was done, and the discussion of this method continues in the text that follows.

steps.title: רבי שמעון asks how the nations could learn a covered Torah
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון challenges רבי יהודה: if the Torah was covered with plaster, how could the nations of the world learn it?
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון said to him: According to what you say, how did the nations of the world learn Torah?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי שמעון attacks רבי יהודה's view from the previous step. If the writing was hidden under plaster, nobody could read it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The assumption is that the Torah was written on the stones so that the nations could learn it too. רבי יהודה said the writing was covered with plaster. That seems to defeat the whole purpose.

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon said to him:
According to your words,
phrases.notes: He means: if the writing was covered with plaster, as רבי יהודה just said.

phrases.english: how did the nations of the world learn Torah?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לוֹ רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן: לִדְבָרֶיךָ, הֵיאַךְ לָמְדוּ אוּמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם תּוֹרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי יהודה's statement in step 11 that the stones were plastered over.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יהודה's claim that the Torah was written on the stones and then covered with plaster.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Covered writing cannot be read, so the nations would have had no way to learn the Torah from the stones.

steps.title: רבי יהודה: the nations peeled off the plaster and copied the Torah
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה answers that ה׳ gave the nations extra understanding. They sent scribes, peeled off the plaster and copied the Torah. Since they had it and did not learn it, their punishment was sealed.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: The Holy One, Blessed be He, gave them extra understanding. They sent their scribes, who peeled off the plaster and copied the writing. Because of this, their sentence to the pit of destruction was sealed, since they should have learned and did not.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהודה defends his view. The plaster did not stop the nations, because they were able to remove it and copy the Torah.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The plaster was not a real barrier, since ה׳ gave the nations the wisdom to get past it. This also explains their punishment. They actually had the Torah in their hands and still chose not to learn it.

phrases.english: He said to him:

phrases.aramaic: בִּינָה יְתֵירָה נָתַן בָּהֶם הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא,
phrases.english: The Holy One, Blessed be He, gave them extra understanding,
and they sent their scribes,
and they peeled off the plaster and copied it.
phrases.notes: והשיאוה literally means 'they carried it off.' Here it means they copied the writing down.

phrases.aramaic: וְעַל דָּבָר זֶה נִתְחַתֵּם גְּזַר דִּינָם
phrases.english: And because of this their sentence was sealed
to the pit of destruction,
because they should have learned and they did not learn.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לוֹ: בִּינָה יְתֵירָה נָתַן בָּהֶם הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי שמעון's challenge from step 12.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explains how the problem was overcome in practice: the nations removed the plaster.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The plaster made the Torah impossible for the nations to read.
steps.terutzMaskana: With extra wisdom from ה׳, the nations peeled off the plaster and copied the Torah, so they are responsible for not learning it.

steps.title: רבי שמעון: the Torah was written on top of the plaster
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון holds that the Torah was written on top of the plaster. Below it they wrote the פסוק 'lest they teach you,' which shows the nations would have been accepted if they did תשובה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון says: They wrote it on top of the plaster, and below they wrote for the nations: 'Lest they teach you to do like all their abominations.' From here you learn that if they had done תשובה, they would have been accepted.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי שמעון now gives his own opinion. The plaster went on first and the Torah was written over it. He adds that a special פסוק was written for the nations to see.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק gives the reason the Canaanite nations were to be destroyed: so they would not teach the Jews their bad ways. If they stopped those ways and did תשובה, that reason would be gone, and they could have stayed.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two opinions. For רבי יהודה, the plaster was on top of the writing. For רבי שמעון, the writing was on top of the plaster.

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon says:
They wrote it on top of the plaster,
and they wrote for them below:
"[Lest] they teach you to do like all etc."
From here you learn
that if they would have repented
they would have accepted them.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר: עַל גַּבֵּי סִיד כְּתָבוּהָ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives רבי שמעון's own view, which disagrees with רבי יהודה's view from steps 11 and 13.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The Torah was written on top of the plaster, along with a פסוק showing that the nations could have done תשובה and been accepted.

steps.title: רבא בר שילא gives the source for רבי שמעון
steps.stepSummary: רבא בר שילא explains רבי שמעון's view from the פסוק 'the peoples shall be as burnings of plaster.' He reads it as saying the nations were punished because of the plaster.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא בר שילא said: What is רבי שמעון's reason? As it is written: 'And the peoples shall be as burnings of plaster.' This means they were punished because of matters of plaster.
steps.whatsHappening: An אמורא brings a פסוק to back up רבי שמעון's opinion about the plaster.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק links the nations' punishment to plaster. According to רבי שמעון, the Torah was written right on the plaster where they could read it. So they were punished over the plaster, meaning the Torah written on it that they ignored.

phrases.english: Rava bar Sheila said:
What is the reason of Rabbi Shimon?
As it is written:
"And the peoples shall be as burnings of plaster"
because of matters of plaster.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא בַּר שֵׁילָא: מַאי טַעְמָא דְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a פסוק source for רבי שמעון's view in step 14.
steps.raayaObject: רבי שמעון's view that the Torah was written on the plaster and the nations were punished for not learning it.
steps.raayaSupportSource: ישעיהו 33:12, 'והיו עמים משרפות סיד,' read as 'because of matters of plaster.'

steps.title: How רבי יהודה reads the plaster verse
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains how רבי יהודה reads the same פסוק. The nations are compared to plaster: just as plaster's only fix is burning, the nations' only fix is burning.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יהודה? He reads it as 'like plaster.' Just as plaster has no fix except burning, so too the nations of the world have no fix except burning.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks how רבי יהודה deals with רבי שמעון's פסוק and answers that he reads it as a comparison.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה does not need the פסוק to be about writing on plaster. For him, the word 'plaster' is a comparison. Plaster is made by burning, and in the same way the nations' end is burning.
steps.whatToRemember: Two views on the stones. רבי יהודה says the writing was under the plaster and the nations peeled it off and copied it. רבי שמעון says the writing was on top of the plaster, with a message that תשובה was possible. Both read 'משרפות סיד' in their own way.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yehuda?
phrases.notes: The גמרא is asking how he explains this פסוק, since for him the Torah was not written on the plaster.

phrases.english: Like plaster:

phrases.aramaic: מָה סִיד אֵין לוֹ תַּקָּנָה אֶלָּא שְׂרֵיפָה
phrases.english: just as plaster has no fix except burning,

phrases.aramaic: אַף אוּמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם אֵין לָהֶם תַּקָּנָה אֶלָּא שְׂרֵיפָה.
phrases.english: so too the nations of the world have no fix except burning.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers how רבי יהודה reads the פסוק that step 15 used for רבי שמעון.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereads the פסוק as a comparison instead of a reason.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The פסוק seems to support only רבי שמעון's view that the nations were punished over the plaster writing.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי יהודה reads the פסוק as comparing the nations to plaster, whose only fix is burning.

steps.title: Which opinion does the ברייתא about repentant כנענים follow?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that reads 'and you take them captive' as including כנענים outside ארץ ישראל, who are accepted if they do תשובה. It asks whose opinion this ברייתא follows.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whose opinion does this ברייתא follow? It teaches that the פסוק 'and you take them captive' comes to include כנענים who live outside ארץ ישראל. If they do תשובה, they are accepted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא and asks which side of the רבי יהודה / רבי שמעון argument it matches. This is a setup question, and the answer comes on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 14, רבי שמעון said the nations would have been accepted if they did תשובה. This ברייתא says the same thing about כנענים outside ארץ ישראל. The גמרא is checking which תנא this ברייתא fits, using the 'they are accepted' idea as the link.

keyTerms.meaning: Whose opinion does this follow? A question asking which רב a teaching matches.
That which is taught in a ברייתא, a teaching of the תנאים that is not in the משנה.
To include. A פסוק is read as adding a case.

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a challenge to anyone yet. The גמרא is only asking which opinion the ברייתא fits. The answer comes on the next amud.

phrases.english: In accordance with whose opinion is
that which is taught in a ברייתא:
"And you take them captive"
comes to include Canaanites who are outside the land,
phrases.notes: Taking captives means not wiping them out, so the ברייתא reads this פסוק as including even these כנענים.

phrases.english: that if they repent,
they are accepted?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After both sides explained the פסוק about plaster, the גמרא now tests which side a ברייתא supports.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which תנא, רבי יהודה or רבי שמעון, does the ברייתא about accepting repentant כנענים follow?
